info.title: OpenAPI For Cargo Insurance
info.description: APIs to insure a single shipment or run a marine open cover for your customers

get.description: Every list of values the cargo endpoints accept: customer roles, transport modes, goods categories, packaging, conditions, characteristics, coverages, extensions, valuation bases, Incoterms, currencies and countries. Each entry has the `value` to send and a `label` to show. Build your dropdowns from this response instead of hard-coding them, so a new value reaches your users without a release on your side.

200.description: The options, one list per key

valuation_bases.label: Invoice value plus freight and other costs (CIF)

post.description:
Registers the business the cargo is insured for, by its commercial registration (CR) number. When the commercial registry knows the business, its legal name and address come from there and the customer is `verified`; anything you send for those fields is ignored. When it does not, the call answers `40031`: send it again with `legal_name` and `address`, and the customer is kept as entered, `unverified`.

Registering a CR number you already registered updates that customer and answers `200` instead of `201`.

role.description: The business's part in the trade. One of the `customer_roles` values from Get the options.

contact.description: The person at the business to contact about its policies.

legal_name.description: Only used when the registry has no record of the CR number.

legal_name_ar.description: Only used when the registry has no record of the CR number.

country.description: Two-letter country code, one of the `countries` values.

address.description: Only used when the registry has no record of the CR number. `street` and `city` are required when it is sent.

200.description: The customer you had already registered, updated

400.description: `40031` when the commercial registry has no record of the CR number and `legal_name` or `address` is missing.

example.message: This commercial registration could not be verified. Send legal_name and address to register the business manually.

post.description:
Asks for a price to insure one shipment. The answer is always `201`; read its `status`:

- `approved`: `quote` holds the price, valid until `quote.valid_until`. Issue the policy from it.
- `referred`: an underwriter has to review the shipment, and `reasons` says why. Read the request again until it is `approved` or `rejected`.
- `rejected`: the shipment cannot be insured, and `reasons` says why.

A quote needs the goods, the route, the value and the cover. The departure date, the carrier and the invoice number are needed to issue a policy but not to quote: send them now if you have them, or later with Issue a policy. `missing_to_issue` lists the ones still missing.

201.description: The quote request, with its decision

reasons: Hazardous goods need an underwriter's review.
Shipments to or from North Korea cannot be insured.

get.description: The quote request as it stands now. Use it to follow a referral: once the underwriter has decided, `status` turns `approved` (and `quote` is filled) or `rejected`.

post.description:
Applies for a marine open cover: a one-year policy that the business declares its shipments under, instead of insuring each on its own. The application describes the goods it ships, the routes, the value it expects to ship in the year and the most any one shipment will be worth.

The answer is always `201`; read its `status`, which works as it does for a single shipment. When it is `approved`, `quote` holds the terms: the rate every declared shipment is charged at (`declaration_rate_percent`) and the deposit paid up front to start the policy (`total_price`, VAT included).

start_date.description: The first day of cover, today or later. The policy runs for one year from this day.

goods.description: The kinds of goods the business ships.

description.description: What the goods are, in plain words.

category.description: The kind of goods. One of the `goods_categories` values from Get the options.

packaging.description: How the goods are packed. One of the `packaging` values from Get the options.

characteristics.description: Anything about the goods that changes the risk. Each one of the `characteristics` values from Get the options.

estimated_annual_value.description: The value the business expects to ship in the year, in `currency`. At least one of the three must be above zero.

currency.description: The currency of the values in the application. One of the `currencies` values from Get the options.

routes.description: The routes the business ships on.

transport_mode.description: How the goods travel on this route. One of the `transport_modes` values from Get the options.

storage_locations.description: Where goods are stored along the way.

max_value_per_shipment.description: The most any one shipment will be worth, in `currency`. A declared shipment above it is referred.

coverage.description: The cover wanted. One of the `coverages` values from Get the options.

extensions.description: Extra cover on top. Each one of the `extensions` values from Get the options.

valuation_basis.description: How the shipment is valued. Defaults to `cif_plus_10`. One of the `valuation_bases` values from Get the options.

first_policy.description: `true` when the business has never held cargo insurance.

post.description:
Accepts an approved quote, for a single shipment or for open cover. The policy comes back unpaid (`status` `0`, `coverage_confirmed` `false`) with a `payment_link`. Send the customer to that page to pay. Once the payment succeeds the policy is issued: it gets its policy number, certificate and tax invoice, and the customer is sent on to your `redirect_url`.

For a single shipment, send in `shipment` whichever of the departure date, the carrier and the invoice number were not on the quote request; the call answers `40033` while any is missing. An open cover needs nothing more than `quote_request_id`.

Calling this again for the same quote before it is paid returns the same policy, updated.

quote_request_id.description: The `id` of an approved quote request or open-cover application.

redirect_url.description: Where to send the customer after they pay. `policyID` anywhere in it is replaced with the policy's id.

201.description: The policy, waiting to be paid for

400.description: `40032` when the request is referred or rejected. `40030` when the quote is past `valid_until`. `40033` when a single shipment still lacks details, listed in `missing_fields`. `40026` when the quote was already issued and paid for; `policy_id` is that policy.

value.message: This request is with an underwriter. Read it again until its status is approved.
The shipment needs these details before it can be issued: departure_date, conveyance.carrier_name, references.invoice_number.
This quote expired on 2026-12-23. Ask for a new one.
This quote was already issued as policy 4.

get.description: The policy as it stands now. While it is unpaid it carries the `payment_link`. Once it is paid for and issued, `coverage_confirmed` is `true`, `provider_policy_id` is the policy number, and `policy_url` and `invoice_url` are the certificate and the tax invoice. An open cover also totals the shipments covered under it in `declarations`.

parameters.description: An open-cover policy that is paid for and issued.

post.description:
Declares one shipment under an open-cover policy. A shipment inside the policy's terms (its goods, its routes and its limit per shipment) is covered at once: `status` is `issued` and `certificate_url` is its certificate. A shipment outside them is `referred` to an underwriter, and `reasons` says why; read the declaration again until it is `issued` or `rejected`.

`premium` is what the shipment costs at the policy's rate. Declared premiums are reported here and totalled on the policy; they are not paid through a payment link.

`shipment.departure_date` has to fall within the policy period.

400.description: `40027` when the open-cover policy is not paid for and issued yet, or is past its last day.

example.message: Shipments can be declared once the open-cover policy is paid for and issued, and until its last day.
